Every basaltic shield volcano is built m.why: The make-up of shield volcanoes is stated directly and often (the textbook contrast with ash-built stratovolcanoes and cinder cones). The class is basaltic shields because Wikipedia notes the term is 'at times' applied to rarer pyroclastic shields built from fragmentary material (Billy Mitchell, Purico), which would be real exceptions to a rule about all shields; basaltic shields, the usual sense, have none.

notes: TBox rule edit: shield volcanoes, built from fluid lava, are given the ash layers of stratovolcanoes and cinder cones, a plausible mix-up. Derivability very_unlikely: stated directly. The rule says 'mainly' and is about make-up, not slope: slope was considered and dropped because some shields (the Galápagos type) have steep upper flanks, a real exception. New members: Trölladyngja and Kollóttadyngja, Icelandic basaltic shields (Wikipedia), little known by name (525 and 70 Dolma mentions). Mauna Loa and Kīlauea are the archetypal shields, so the world where they stop counting as shield volcanoes is lopsided but kept. The two background queries ask well-known members whose property a model likely also stores by name (README, TBox). For each member, one world keeps the stored property and the member stops counting as a member of the class; the other keeps the membership and applies the edited rule. The two members' choices are independent, so the worlds combine them (four). Lopsided worlds are kept (README Decisions 4). Changed in verification: (1) the class is narrowed from shield volcanoes to basaltic shield volcanoes, because Wikipedia's Shield volcano article names pyroclastic shields (Billy Mitchell, Purico) built from fragmentary material, real exceptions to 'every shield volcano is built mainly from fluid lava'; Mauna Loa and Kīlauea are basaltic shields. 'Basaltic' leans toward lava but does not state the answer (basaltic ash and cinder cones exist), an accepted R2 risk. (2) The new members Erta Ale (famous lava lake, 'Erta Ale AND lava' 3,390 approximate) and Piton de la Fournaise ('AND lava flows' 1,232) were replaced by obscure Icelandic shields, since their lava make-up is likely stored by name. The either-or questions take one value for granted; since 2026-10-31 this is stated as a bridge of the two well-known-member queries ('A volcano built mainly from fluid lava flows is not built mainly from layers of volcanic ash.'), which is why each world gives up either the membership or the stored value (formal check, FINDINGS B3/C3).
